chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Hazza', who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a man asked me, 'What did your creditor do?' I said, 'That one is the son of the sexually active (immoral) woman.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) looked at me with a harsh look. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, he is a Magian. His mother is his sister.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Or is that not (considered a valid) marriage in their religion?'

key_terms.ابْنُ الْفَاعِلَةِ: son of the sexually active woman (a term for illegitimate birth)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on slandering non-Muslims based on their marriage practices?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imam’s precise scrutiny of linguistic slander (*ghibah* or *namima*) by challenging the derogatory label 'Ibn al-Fa'ila' applied to a Magian creditor. The Imam highlights that within Zoroastrian endogamous marriage customs, where a man may marry his sister, the term is technically descriptive rather than purely insulting, thereby refining the criteria for valid slander against non-Muslims. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on contextual accuracy in social discourse and the specific legal status of *Ahl al-Kitab* and Magians in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Al Hassan Al Haza’a who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so a man said to me, ‘What did your creditor do?’ I said, ‘That one is a son of a ‘sexually active (immoral) woman’ . So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> looked at me with a harsh look. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! He is a Magian. His mother is his sister’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Or is that not (considered a valid) marriage in their religion?’
